title: Find the Middle Index in Array
summary: Determine the first index in an array where the sum of elements to the left equals the sum of elements to the right, considering the leftmost index as 0 and the rightmost index as the array's length minus one, returning -1 if no such index exists.
statement: Determine the first index in an array where the sum of elements to the left equals the sum of elements to the right, considering the leftmost index as 0 and the rightmost index as the array's length minus one, returning -1 if no such index exists.
constraints: nums contains 1 through 100 integers from -1000 through 1000.
At a middle index, the sum strictly left equals the sum strictly right.
Return the leftmost middle index, or -1 if none exists.
hints: Maintain the sum on each side while scanning once.
Begin with the total on the right; remove the current value before comparing, then add it to the left after comparing.
right=sum(nums), left=0; for i,x: right-=x; compare; left+=x.
At comparison time the maintained totals contain exactly the elements strictly before and strictly after the current index; the first equality is therefore the required answer.
editorial: At comparison time the maintained totals contain exactly the elements strictly before and strictly after the current index; the first equality is therefore the required answer.

tests.explanation: At index three, both sides sum to four.
At index two, the left sum is zero and the empty right side also sums to zero.
